title: Chunk serialization and caller-memory deserialization
scope: Versioned UInt32 and generic chunk packets on .NET 10 x64, with 1, 4, and 16 channels over uniform, sparse, clustered, and random level-5 data.
question: Can chunk serialization and deserialization materially reduce latency and allocations while preserving packet compatibility and accepting reusable caller-owned memory?

summary.headline: Allocation-free 16-channel envelope parsing reduced mean latency by 75.3% versus owned construction; full validation remains an explicit second step.

hypotheses.claim: Repeated serialized-length calculation adds a descriptor traversal to every write.
hypotheses.prediction: SerializedLength becomes O(1) without changing packet bytes.
hypotheses.falsification: Changed length or packet output, or construction cost that defeats write reuse.
hypotheses.change: Cache the checked packet length when the immutable chunk is constructed.
hypotheses.result: Length and packet equality tests pass; the traversal is removed, although its isolated latency was not separately benchmarked.
risks: Adds one integer field to owned chunks.

hypotheses.claim: Owned deserialization repeats semantic traversal to derive IsEmpty after structural validation.
hypotheses.prediction: Exact empty-state parity with less tree traversal.
hypotheses.falsification: Any IsEmpty mismatch across uniform, tree, or dense encodings.
hypotheses.change: Derive empty state from validated canonical storage kinds and dense bytes.
hypotheses.result: Existing and new round-trip tests preserve IsEmpty; isolated timing remains mixed by pattern.
risks: Depends on the existing canonical-tree validation invariant.

hypotheses.claim: One general contiguous copy is faster than per-channel packet reconstruction.
hypotheses.prediction: At least 15% faster across loaded packets.
hypotheses.result: Rejected for large random packets; the 16-channel case reached 1.917 ms versus 66.354 us screening control.

hypotheses.claim: A stack-bound packet view provides allocation-free caller-memory deserialization.
hypotheses.prediction: 0 B allocated and materially lower envelope-parse latency.
hypotheses.falsification: Any allocation, lifetime ambiguity, or malformed-envelope acceptance.
hypotheses.change: Add OctreeChunkSpan and OctreeChunkSpan<T> with envelope parsing and explicit full validation.
hypotheses.result: 0 B in all 12 workloads; envelope parsing improved 65.4-99.99% versus owned construction.
risks: Caller must keep packet memory alive and immutable.

hypotheses.claim: Retained packet identity accelerates loaded-chunk serialization.
hypotheses.mechanism: Bypass header reconstruction for bounded packets
hypotheses.prediction: At least 15% faster with no large-packet regression.
hypotheses.change: Retain exact packet ReadOnlyMemory and use one copy only when length is at most 64 KiB.
hypotheses.result: Small 4/16-channel uniform and clustered packets improved 51.2-87.0%; unbounded copying was rejected.
risks: Large packets intentionally retain the existing per-channel path.

hypotheses.claim: Stack-only views can remove owned descriptor allocation without unsafe lifetime transfer.
hypotheses.prediction: 0 B allocated with explicit caller-memory lifetime documentation.
hypotheses.falsification: Escaping spans, hidden allocation, or ambiguous ownership.
hypotheses.change: Keep only the packet span, levels, and channel count in the view.
hypotheses.result: Allocation diagnoser reports 0 B; ref-struct lifetime is compiler-enforced.
risks: Random channel access scans preceding length fields.

hypotheses.claim: Dense empty-state detection can use raw validated bytes instead of a spatial query.
hypotheses.prediction: Exact bitwise-empty semantics and reduced query overhead.
hypotheses.falsification: Bitwise nonzero values classified as empty.
hypotheses.change: Use IndexOfAnyExcept on .NET 10+ with a scalar netstandard fallback.
hypotheses.result: Correctness passed for all target frameworks; end-to-end timing is pattern-dependent.

hypotheses.claim: UInt32 and generic packets can expose equivalent reuse APIs without format divergence.
hypotheses.prediction: Identical ownership and validation behavior for both packet versions.
hypotheses.change: Add generic view, capacity, copy, retained-data, and empty-state paths.
hypotheses.result: Generic exact-value, round-trip, and structural validation tests pass on net8.0, net10.0, and net11.0.

hypotheses.claim: 64 KiB segmented copies avoid the runtime's large-copy regime.
hypotheses.prediction: Within 5% of corrected control at 1, 4, and 16 random channels.
hypotheses.change: Screened repeated 64 KiB span copies over the retained packet.
hypotheses.result: Rejected: +127.2% at one channel and +53.8% at sixteen channels.

retainedChanges: Reusable caller destinations through GetMaximumSerializedLength and TryCopyEncodedTo.
Allocation-free OctreeChunkSpan and OctreeChunkSpan<T> views over caller-owned packet memory.
Separate inexpensive envelope parsing from explicit full structural validation.
Retain exact loaded packet memory and expose it through TryGetSerializedData.
Use the retained-packet copy fast path only for packets at or below 64 KiB.
Cache immutable serialized length and derive IsEmpty from validated storage metadata.
decisions: Untrusted borrowed packets must call IsWellFormed before channel-tree use.
Large loaded packets retain per-channel serialization; unrestricted and segmented copies failed the regression guardrail.
The packet wire formats remain version 1 and version 2 without byte changes.
correctness: 924 target-specific tests passed: 307 net8.0, 308 net10.0, and 309 net11.0.
Reusable destination failure returns false, writes zero bytes, and preserves the destination.
Loaded-packet aliasing, overlap rejection, exact packet copying, generic exact values, truncation rejection, and zero allocation are covered.
Local NuGet package inspection confirmed assemblies and XML documentation for netstandard2.1, net10.0, and net11.0 plus required package documents.
validityThreats: BenchmarkDotNet ShortRun uses three measured iterations; nanosecond-scale confidence intervals can be broad.
Exploratory epoch E-001 overlapped a subsequently introduced host lock and used misleading multi-channel pattern perturbations; it is excluded from acceptance decisions.
The E-002 manual serialization control omitted legacy safety work, so only candidate wins against it are treated as conservative screening evidence.
Envelope parsing is intentionally not equivalent to full structural validation; the report labels these tiers separately.
Full borrowed validation regressed in 3 of 12 workloads, including +8.8% for four-channel clustered data; callers choose it primarily for zero allocation and caller-memory ownership.
No generated-code claim was retained, so disassembly was not required.
reproduction: Acquire D:\Temp\BenchmarkLock.txt atomically and verify the host has no active build, test, profiler, or benchmark process.
From src\Tedd.Voxtree.Benchmark run the E-002 command recorded in README.md.
For H-009 run: dotnet run -c Release -f net10.0 --no-build --project Tedd.Voxtree.Benchmark.csproj -- --filter '*SerializeLoaded*Random*' --job short --artifacts '<run>\raw\final-segmented'
Run: dotnet pack src\Tedd.Voxtree\Tedd.Voxtree.csproj -c Release --no-build -o artifacts\packages
Release the lock only after every child process exits.
